finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. The OWNER check is never enforced, so any authenticated user can wipe any tenant. The sibling export() uses checkRole(), which does throw, so the two endpoints are inconsistent.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, with any roles and an attacker-chosen tenant path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive operation that deletes tenant data.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for POST /tenants/{t}/wipe
requireRole(u,"OWNER") returns a boolean, and the return value is ignored
requireRole only does roles().contains(role) and never throws, per its own Javadoc

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the ignored requireRole() call. No other authorization check, exception, or middleware is visible in the repo, which contains only this file. Compare export() at line 32, which uses the throwing checkRole().

verdict.guard_found: requireRole() at src/Admin.java:14 only returns a boolean and never throws. Its result is discarded at line 26, so it blocks nothing. checkRole() at line 18 does throw, but only export() at line 32 calls it.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole (defined at :14-16, returns a boolean and does not throw) as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike export() at :32, which uses the throwing checkRole() at :18-22.

finding.claim: Authorization is a global role check with no tenant scoping. An OWNER of one tenant can export, and once AUTH-1 is fixed can also wipe, any other tenant by changing the {t} path parameter (cross-tenant IDOR). The tenant argument is never compared to the user's own tenant or memberships.
finding.source: An authenticated user holding the OWNER role in any tenant, supplying an arbitrary tenant id in the path.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) and repo.wipe(tenant), which operate on another tenant's data.

repo.export(tenant) uses the attacker-supplied tenant id

finding.guards_checked: checkRole() verifies the role string only. No tenant-membership check exists in this file. Any controller or middleware outside the repo could not be examined, so this is a candidate.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws SecurityException, but it checks only the global role string. No tenant comparison or membership check exists anywhere in the repo.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:32 calls checkRole(u,"OWNER"), which only tests u.roles() (line 19). User (line 4) has no tenant field, so the attacker-supplied tenant reaches repo.export(tenant) at line 33 unchecked. Any OWNER can therefore export any tenant.
